q: The Earnings Budget of the Railways is framed mainly on the basis of:

options.A: The earnings of the previous year, repeated without change
options.B: The anticipated volume of passenger and goods traffic and the fares and rates expected to be in force
options.C: The total plan outlay of the year
options.D: The recommendations of the Railway Convention Committee

e: The Earnings Budget is framed mainly on the basis of the anticipated volume of passenger and goods traffic and the fares and rates expected to be in force during the year.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The estimates of earnings are initially framed by the executive (operating/commercial) departments.
2. The estimates so framed are scrutinised by the Accounts Department before they are adopted in the Budget.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the estimates of earnings are initially framed by the executive (operating/commercial) departments, and the Accounts Department scrutinises them before they are adopted in the Budget.

q: Under the rule of lapse, the balance of a grant remaining unspent at the close of the financial year:

options.A: Is automatically available for expenditure in the following year
options.B: Lapses and is not available for expenditure in the following year
options.C: Is transferred to the Development Fund
options.D: Is carried forward as a suspense balance

e: Under the rule of lapse, the balance of a grant remaining unspent at the close of the financial year lapses and is not available for expenditure in the following year.

q: After the abolition of the August Review, the budget — including the working expenses estimates — is formally reviewed during the year at:

options.C: No stage; the original estimates remain unaltered throughout the year
options.D: Two stages — the Revised Estimates stage (September) and the Final Modification stage (January)

e: After the abolition of the August Review, the budget is formally reviewed at two stages - the Revised Estimates stage in September and the Final Modification stage in January.

q: The Outcome Budget, presented along with the Budget documents, primarily seeks to:

options.A: List the works included in the Pink Book
options.B: Relate the financial outlays provided to the physical outcomes and deliverables expected from them
options.C: Show the suspense balances of the Railways
options.D: Fix the Primary Units of expenditure

e: The Outcome Budget primarily seeks to relate the financial outlays provided to the physical outcomes and deliverables expected from them, shifting the focus from expenditure to results.

q: The Outcome Budget was first introduced in the Union Budget for the year:
e: The Outcome Budget was first introduced in the Union Budget for the year 2005-06 and has since been presented along with the Budget documents.

q: Which of the following does NOT form part of the financing of the Railways' annual plan outlay?

options.B: Internal resources of the Railways (Railway Funds)
options.D: Advances from the Contingency Fund of India

e: The annual plan outlay is financed by Gross Budgetary Support, the Railways' internal resources (Railway Funds) and Extra Budgetary Resources; advances from the Contingency Fund of India form no part of this financing.

q: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) raises resources for the Railways mainly through:

options.B: Loans from the World Bank only
options.D: Issue of bonds in the capital market

e: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation raises resources for the Railways mainly through the issue of bonds in the capital market, and deploys them for rolling stock and projects.

q: The Capital Fund of the Railways is utilised mainly for:

options.A: Financing asset-creating (capital) works out of the Railways' internal resources

e: The Capital Fund of the Railways is utilised mainly for financing capital works chargeable to Capital, such as capacity-augmentation works, when the budgetary support available under the Capital head is inadequate.

q: The Demands for Grants are voted exclusively by the:

options.C: Both Houses of Parliament sitting jointly

e: The Demands for Grants are voted exclusively by the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha may discuss the Budget but has no power to vote the Demands.

q: The practice of putting all the outstanding Demands for Grants to the vote of the Lok Sabha together on the last allotted day is known as:
e: The practice of putting all the outstanding Demands for Grants to the vote of the Lok Sabha together on the last allotted day is known as the Guillotine.

q: A 'token cut' motion moved during the discussion on the Demands for Grants proposes a reduction of:
e: A token cut motion proposes a reduction of Rs 100 in the Demand; it is moved to draw attention to a specific grievance rather than to effect a real economy.

q: The proposals submitted by the zonal railways for works to be included in the following year's Works Programme are known as the:
e: The proposals submitted by the zonal railways for works to be included in the following year's Works Programme are known as the Preliminary Works Programme; the approved programme becomes the Final Works Programme.

q: In the Pink Book, works costing more than the prescribed limit are shown individually and are known as:
e: In the Pink Book, works costing more than the prescribed limit are shown individually with full details and are known as itemised works, as against lumpsum or umbrella provisions.

q: The works finally approved for inclusion in the Works Programme are listed in the Pink Book arranged:

options.A: Alphabetically by the name of the work

e: The works finally approved for the Works Programme are listed in the Pink Book arranged Plan Head-wise, grouping together all works of the same investment category.

q: Transfer transactions which involve no actual receipt or payment of cash and are mere book adjustments are known as:
e: Transfer transactions which involve no actual receipt or payment of cash and are mere book adjustments are known as transfers without financial effect.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Transfers without financial effect are also carried out through journal (transfer) entries in the books.
2. Such transfers do not affect the cash balance of the Railways with the Reserve Bank of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: transfers without financial effect are carried out through journal (transfer) entries, and since no cash moves, they do not affect the Railways' cash balance with the Reserve Bank of India.

q: An error of classification between the Revenue and Capital heads which comes to notice after the accounts of the year have been closed is rectified:

options.A: By reopening the accounts of the closed year
options.B: In the accounts of the year in which the error is noticed
options.C: Never; it is left uncorrected in the books

e: An error of classification between Revenue and Capital heads noticed after the year's accounts are closed is rectified in the accounts of the year in which the error is noticed, not by reopening the closed accounts.

q: The Traffic Book in railway accounts is principally concerned with:

options.A: The day-to-day booking of traffic receipts at stations
options.B: The apportionment of through-traffic earnings among the railways concerned and the adjustment of the results thereof
options.D: The preparation of the earnings budget

e: The Traffic Book is principally concerned with the apportionment of through-traffic earnings among the railways over which the traffic passed, and the adjustment of the apportioned results between them.

q: To accommodate year-end adjustments, the Account Current for the month of March is rendered in two parts, namely:
e: To accommodate year-end adjustments, the March Account Current is rendered in two parts - March (Preliminary) and March (Final) - so that later adjustments can still be included before the year closes.

q: General Superintendence and Services (erstwhile Demand No. 3) is classified under Major Head 3002 as Sub-Major Head:
e: General Superintendence and Services (erstwhile Demand No. 3) is Sub-Major Head 01 under Major Head 3002, the first in the sequence mapping Demands 3 to 14 onto Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12.

q: Repairs and Maintenance of Motive Power (erstwhile Demand No. 5) is classified under Major Head 3002 as Sub-Major Head:
e: Repairs and Maintenance of Motive Power (erstwhile Demand No. 5) is Sub-Major Head 03 under Major Head 3002, in the sequence mapping Demands 3 to 14 onto Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12.

q: Repairs and Maintenance of Carriages and Wagons (erstwhile Demand No. 6) is classified under Major Head 3002 as Sub-Major Head:
e: Repairs and Maintenance of Carriages and Wagons (erstwhile Demand No. 6) is Sub-Major Head 04 under Major Head 3002, in the sequence mapping Demands 3 to 14 onto Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12.

q: Operating Expenses — Rolling Stock and Equipment (erstwhile Demand No. 8) is classified under Major Head 3002 as Sub-Major Head:
e: Operating Expenses - Rolling Stock and Equipment (erstwhile Demand No. 8) is Sub-Major Head 06 under Major Head 3002, in the sequence mapping Demands 3 to 14 onto Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12.

q: Operating Expenses — Traffic (erstwhile Demand No. 9) is classified under Major Head 3002 as Sub-Major Head:
e: Operating Expenses - Traffic (erstwhile Demand No. 9) is Sub-Major Head 07 under Major Head 3002, in the sequence mapping Demands 3 to 14 onto Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12.

q: Miscellaneous Working Expenses (erstwhile Demand No. 12) are classified under Major Head 3002 as Sub-Major Head:
e: Miscellaneous Working Expenses (erstwhile Demand No. 12) are Sub-Major Head 10 under Major Head 3002, in the sequence mapping Demands 3 to 14 onto Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12.

q: In the investment (Plan Head) classification, Gauge Conversion is Plan Head:
e: In the investment (Plan Head) classification, Gauge Conversion is Plan Head 14.

q: In the investment (Plan Head) classification, Doubling of railway lines is Plan Head:
e: In the investment (Plan Head) classification, Doubling of railway lines is Plan Head 15.

q: Traffic Facilities — yard remodelling and other traffic facility works — are classified under Plan Head:
e: Traffic Facilities - yard remodelling and other traffic facility works - are classified under Plan Head 16 in the investment classification.

q: Works of computerisation on the Railways are classified under Plan Head:
e: Works of computerisation on the Railways are classified under Plan Head 17 in the investment classification.

q: Road Safety Works relating to level crossings are classified under Plan Head:
e: Road Safety Works relating to level crossings are classified under Plan Head 29; road over-bridge and under-bridge works fall under Plan Head 30.

q: Bridge Works, including tunnel works and approaches, are classified under Plan Head:
e: Bridge Works, including tunnel works and approaches, are classified under Plan Head 32 in the investment classification.

q: Signalling and Telecommunication works are classified under Plan Head:
e: Signalling and Telecommunication works are classified under Plan Head 33 in the investment classification.

q: Construction of staff quarters is classified under Plan Head:
e: Construction of staff quarters is classified under Plan Head 51 in the investment classification.

q: Works which are not covered by any specific Plan Head are classified under 'Other Specified Works', which is Plan Head:
e: Works not covered by any specific Plan Head are classified under 'Other Specified Works', which is Plan Head 64, the residual head of the investment classification.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Plan Head classification, Stores Suspense is Plan Head 71 and Manufacturing Suspense is Plan Head 72.
2. Miscellaneous Advances (Capital) are classified under Plan Head 73.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Stores Suspense is Plan Head 71 and Manufacturing Suspense is Plan Head 72, and Miscellaneous Advances (Capital) are classified under Plan Head 73.

q: The dividend payable by the Railways to General Revenues (before it was discontinued) was computed on the basis of:

options.A: Gross traffic earnings of the year
options.C: Net revenue remaining after meeting working expenses
options.D: The total value of the Block Account assets created in the year

e: The dividend payable to General Revenues was computed on the basis of the Capital-at-charge of the Railways, applying the prescribed rate to the total capital invested.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The rate of dividend payable by the Railways to General Revenues was determined on the basis of the recommendations of the Railway Convention Committee.
2. Capital expenditure on certain categories of works, such as strategic lines, was exempt from dividend liability, and a subsidy was borne by General Revenues in respect of such capital.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the dividend rate was determined on the Railway Convention Committee's recommendations, and capital on categories like strategic lines was exempt from dividend, with a subsidy borne by General Revenues for such capital.

q: Where the net revenue of the Railways in a year was insufficient to meet the full dividend liability to General Revenues, the unpaid portion of the dividend was carried to the:
e: Where the net revenue was insufficient to meet the full dividend liability, the unpaid portion was carried to the Deferred Dividend Liability Account, to be discharged in a later year.

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes 'Capital-at-charge' from the 'Block Account'?

options.A: The two expressions mean exactly the same thing and are interchangeable
options.B: Capital-at-charge represents the assets of the Railways, while the Block Account represents the corresponding liability
options.C: The Block Account includes only those assets which are financed from the Capital Fund
options.D: Capital-at-charge is the capital invested in the Railways, shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet, while the Block Account represents the corresponding assets

e: Capital-at-charge is the capital invested in the Railways, shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet, while the Block Account represents the corresponding assets created out of that capital.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Block Account in the railway accounts exhibits the assets at their original cost.
2. Depreciation of railway assets is provided for through appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, and not by writing down the Block Account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Block Account exhibits the assets at their original cost, and depreciation is provided through appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, not by writing down the Block Account.

q: In the Balance Sheet of the Railways, the accumulated balances of the Railway Funds — Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund, Pension Fund and the like — are shown on the:

options.C: Neither side, as the funds are kept wholly outside the Balance Sheet
options.D: Assets side only, as investments of the funds

e: In the Railways' Balance Sheet, the accumulated balances of the Railway Funds are shown on the liabilities side, as they are amounts held for the purposes of the respective funds.

q: The cash balance of the Railways held as 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' appears in the Balance Sheet of the Railways on the:

options.C: It does not appear in the Balance Sheet at all
options.D: Both sides of the Balance Sheet

e: The cash balance held as 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' is an asset of the Railways, so it appears on the assets side of the Balance Sheet.

q: Expenditure on services which are common to both new construction and open-line working — such as general administration and supervision — is allocated between Capital and Revenue:

options.D: In the proportions prescribed in the rules/codes for such allocation

e: Expenditure on services common to both new construction and open-line working, such as general administration and supervision, is allocated between Capital and Revenue in the proportions prescribed in the rules and codes.

q:
Consider the following statements about reconciliation of accounts:
1. The figures in the General Books of the Accounts Office are agreed with the records of the executive departments only once, at the time of the annual closing of accounts.
2. Differences brought out by such agreement are investigated and set right through transfer entries.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is wrong: agreement of General Books figures with executive records is a regular, periodic exercise, not one done only at the annual closing. Statement 2 is correct: differences so found are investigated and set right through transfer entries.

q: Amendments and corrections to the classification of accounts — the list of major, minor and other heads contained in the Finance Code — are issued by the Railway Board through:
e: Amendments and corrections to the classification of accounts in the Finance Code are issued by the Railway Board through Correction Slips, which update the list of major, minor and other heads.

q: Transactions of the Railways with the Pay and Accounts Offices of other Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, pending settlement, are passed through the suspense head:
e: Transactions of the Railways with the Pay and Accounts Offices of other Ministries and Departments, pending settlement, are passed through the suspense head PAO Suspense.

q: Adjustments of transactions between the Railways and the State Governments/Accountants General are routed through the suspense head:
e: Adjustments of transactions between the Railways and the State Governments or Accountants General are routed through the suspense head AG Suspense, pending settlement with the other side.

q: Amounts due to the Railways from outside parties for services rendered by the Railways, pending realisation, are debited to the suspense head:
e: Amounts due to the Railways from outside parties for services rendered, pending realisation, are debited to the suspense head Demands Recoverable, so that their recovery remains under watch.

q: Earnest money and security deposits received from contractors and other parties are held in the railway accounts under:

options.A: The 'Deposits' head, among the Debt heads
options.B: Sundry other earnings of the Railways
options.C: Miscellaneous revenue receipts of the year

e: Earnest money and security deposits received from contractors and other parties are held under the 'Deposits' head among the Debt heads, since the money belongs to the depositors and is repayable to them.

q: Advances made by the Railways which are recoverable or adjustable in due course are initially held under the suspense head:
e: Advances recoverable or adjustable in due course are first debited to the Miscellaneous Advances suspense head, where they are watched until cleared by recovery or adjustment to the final head.

q: The transactions of a railway are broadly divided into three categories, namely:

options.A: Revenue transactions, Capital transactions and Debt transactions
options.B: Cash transactions, Cheque transactions and Bill transactions
options.C: Local transactions, Through transactions and Foreign transactions
options.D: Cash transactions, Transfer transactions and Remittance transactions

e: Railway transactions are classified by their mode of settlement: cash transactions involve actual cash, transfer transactions are book adjustments without cash, and remittance transactions are movements between accounting units.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An advance from the Contingency Fund of India can be taken to meet urgent unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation of the expenditure by Parliament.
2. Such an advance is recouped to the Contingency Fund after the expenditure has been authorised through a supplementary grant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: the Contingency Fund exists to meet urgent unforeseen expenditure pending Parliament's authorisation, and the advance is recouped to the Fund once the expenditure is authorised through a supplementary grant.

q: The 'Budget' of the Government of India is the Annual Financial Statement presented to Parliament under Article:
e: Article 112 requires the Annual Financial Statement of estimated receipts and expenditure, which is the Budget, to be laid before Parliament every year.

q: The Appropriation Bill, which authorises withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India, is provided for under Article:
e: Article 114 provides for the Appropriation Bill, introduced after the Demands are voted, to authorise withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Finance Accounts present the total receipts and disbursements of the year under the respective major heads of account.
2. The Appropriation Accounts of the Railways are prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is true: the Finance Accounts present total receipts and disbursements under the respective major heads. Statement 2 is false: the Railways' Appropriation Accounts are prepared by the Railways themselves, not by the CAG, who only audits them.

q:
Consider the following statements about E-Recon:
1. Under E-Recon, acceptance of an inter-railway transfer transaction by the respondent railway is no longer necessary, since the advice is sent electronically.
2. E-Recon enables the online monitoring of transfer transactions which remain unmatched or unaccepted.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: the respondent railway's acceptance of a transfer transaction is still required; E-Recon only transmits the advice electronically. Statement 2 is true: unmatched or unaccepted transfers can be monitored online.

q: The full form of 'IPAS', the integrated application used on the Railways for payroll and accounts work, is:
e: IPAS stands for Integrated Payroll and Accounting System, the integrated application used on the Railways for payroll and accounts work.

q: Under IPAS, the functions brought together in a single integrated system include:

options.D: Payroll, together with the billing, books and budget functions of the Accounts Department

e: IPAS brings payroll together with the billing, books and budget functions of the Accounts Department into a single integrated system, rather than covering any one function alone.

q:
Consider the following statements about the closing of monthly accounts:
1. After the accounts of a month have been closed, further entries may be passed in that month at any time during the same financial year.
2. Rectifications relating to a month whose accounts have been closed are carried out through entries in a subsequent month whose accounts are still open.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: once a month's accounts are closed, no further entries can be passed in that month. Statement 2 is true: rectifications are carried out through entries in a subsequent month whose accounts are still open.

q: After the closure of the March (Final) accounts of a financial year, the annual compilations prepared from the closed accounts are:

options.A: The Appropriation Accounts and the Finance Accounts, including the Balance Sheet
options.B: The Revised Estimates for that year
options.C: The Pink Book for that year
options.D: The Outcome Budget for that year

e: After the March (Final) accounts are closed, the annual compilations prepared are the Appropriation Accounts and the Finance Accounts, including the Balance Sheet of the railway.

q: At the close of the financial year, officers who operate suspense heads are required to furnish to the Accounts Office a certificate relating to:

options.A: The budget allotment required for the next year
options.C: The earnings of the units under them
options.D: The review, and the correctness, of the outstanding suspense balances under the heads operated by them

e: At the close of the year, officers operating suspense heads must certify that the outstanding balances under their heads have been reviewed and are correct, so that old or fictitious items do not accumulate.

q: The gross earnings of the Railways are classified broadly under three categories, namely:

options.A: Local earnings, Through earnings and Foreign earnings
options.B: Coaching earnings, Goods earnings and Traffic Suspense
options.C: Coaching earnings, Goods earnings and Sundry other earnings
options.D: Passenger earnings, Freight earnings and Parcel earnings only

e: Gross railway earnings are classified under three broad heads: Coaching earnings, Goods earnings and Sundry other earnings.

q: A transfer (journal) adjustment in the railway accounts is authorised and recorded through a document known as a:
e: A transfer adjustment, being a book entry without cash movement, is authorised and recorded through a Transfer Entry Order (TEO).

q: The total capital outlay as shown in the accounts — the Block Account — is periodically agreed and reconciled with the:

options.A: Pink Book maintained in the Railway Board
options.B: Budget Register of the Accounts Office
options.C: Asset Registers maintained by the executive departments
options.D: Contractor's ledgers maintained by the executive departments

e: The Block Account shows the total capital outlay; it is periodically agreed with the Asset Registers maintained by the executive departments to confirm that the assets recorded actually exist and are accounted for.

q: Repairs and Maintenance of Plant and Equipment (erstwhile Demand No. 7) is classified under Major Head 3002 as Sub-Major Head:
e: Under Major Head 3002, Repairs and Maintenance of Plant and Equipment (the erstwhile Demand No. 7) is classified as Sub-Major Head 05.

q: In the investment (Plan Head) classification, 'Leased Assets — payment of the capital component of lease charges' is Plan Head:
e: Capital expenditure on leased assets, representing the capital component of lease charges payable to IRFC, is classified under Plan Head 22, "Leased Assets".

q: Electrification Projects are classified under Plan Head:
e: Electrification projects, covering railway electrification works, are classified under Plan Head 36 in the investment classification.

q: Traction Distribution Works are classified under Plan Head:
e: Traction distribution works, such as overhead equipment and related distribution assets, are classified under Plan Head 37.

q: Machinery and Plant is classified under Plan Head:
e: Machinery and Plant, covering workshop and other machinery, is classified under Plan Head 41.

q: Amenities for staff are classified under Plan Head:
e: Amenities for staff, such as staff welfare facilities, are classified under Plan Head 52.

q: Training and Human Resource Development works are classified under Plan Head:
e: Training and Human Resource Development works are classified under Plan Head 65.

q: Metropolitan Transport Projects are classified under Plan Head:
e: Metropolitan Transport Projects in metropolitan cities are classified under Plan Head 81.

q: In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, transactions under the suspense heads are classified under Major Head:
e: In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, suspense transactions are classified under Major Head 8658, "Suspense Accounts".

q: In the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' is Major Head:
e: Major Head 8675 is "Deposits with Reserve Bank", recording the balance of Government money held with the RBI.

q: The detailed classification of railway accounts — the lists of Major Heads, Sub-Major Heads, Minor Heads and Primary Units — is prescribed in the:

options.A: Indian Railway Accounts Code, Volume I
options.B: Indian Railway Finance Code, Volume I
options.D: Indian Railway Finance Code, Volume II

e: The detailed lists of Major Heads, Sub-Major Heads, Minor Heads and Primary Units of railway classification are prescribed in the appendices to the Indian Railway Finance Code, Volume II.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the railway classification of accounts, the Major, Sub-Major and Minor Heads represent the functional classification of expenditure.
2. The Primary Units represent the object (economic) classification of expenditure.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: the Major, Sub-Major and Minor Heads give the functional classification (what the money is spent on), while the Primary Units give the object or economic classification (the nature of the item of expenditure).

q: The Special Railway Safety Fund (SRSF), set up in 2001-02, had a corpus of:
e: The Special Railway Safety Fund set up in 2001-02 had a corpus of Rs 17,000 crore, built up over its initial years.

q: The Special Railway Safety Fund (SRSF) was created primarily to:

options.A: Finance construction of new lines in backward areas
options.C: Wipe out the arrears of replacement and renewal of over-aged safety-related assets such as track, bridges and signalling gear

e: The SRSF was created to wipe out the accumulated arrears of replacement and renewal of over-aged safety-related assets like track, bridges and signalling gear, which ordinary funds could not clear.

q: The Development Fund of the Railways is credited with appropriations made out of:

options.A: The working expenses of the year

e: The Development Fund meets expenditure on passenger amenities, staff welfare and similar works, and is credited with appropriations made out of the surplus of the Railways after dividend and other charges.

q: Appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund are assessed with reference to:

options.A: The original cost of the asset and its prescribed (codal) life
options.B: The current market value of the asset
options.C: The gross earnings of the year
options.D: The dividend liability of the Railways

e: Appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund are assessed with reference to the original cost of each asset and its prescribed (codal) life, so that the fund accumulates enough to replace the asset at the end of its life.

q: Deposits received by the Railways which remain unclaimed for more than the prescribed period are treated as lapsed deposits and credited to the revenue of the Railways. The prescribed period is:
e: Deposits remaining unclaimed for more than three years are treated as lapsed deposits and credited to railway revenue, as the likelihood of a valid claim after that period is treated as extinguished for accounting purposes.

q: The Demands for Grants, on which the Lok Sabha votes the expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, are provided for in the Constitution under Article:
e: Article 113 lays down the procedure for Demands for Grants, under which the estimates of expenditure from the Consolidated Fund are submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha.

q: Under the Constitution, no Demand for a Grant can be made except on the recommendation of:

options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Article 113 provides that no Demand for a Grant shall be made except on the recommendation of the President, signifying the executive's responsibility for the estimates.

q: Supplementary, additional and excess grants are provided for in the Constitution under Article:
e: Article 115 covers supplementary, additional and excess grants, needed when the authorised amount proves insufficient, a new service arises, or expenditure has exceeded the grant.

q: A 'Vote of Credit' is granted by Parliament when:

options.A: Expenditure for a part of the year has to be authorised pending the passing of the full Budget
options.B: Expenditure already incurred exceeds the grant for a service
options.C: The amount authorised for a service proves insufficient during the year
options.D: Owing to the magnitude or the indefinite character of the service, the demand cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in the Budget

e: A Vote of Credit is granted when, owing to the magnitude or indefinite character of a service (such as a war-like emergency), the demand cannot be stated with the usual Budget details, so Parliament votes a lump sum.

q: The Constitution lays down that no money shall be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India except:

options.B: With the sanction of the Finance Minister
options.C: On the recommendation of the Estimates Committee
options.D: Under an order of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Article 266(3) lays down that no moneys shall be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India except under appropriation made by law.

q: Article 112 of the Constitution requires the Annual Financial Statement to distinguish expenditure on ______ from other expenditure:
e: Article 112 requires the Annual Financial Statement to distinguish expenditure on revenue account from other expenditure, so that the revenue and capital position is separately visible.

q: The Contingency Fund of India is established under Article ___ of the Constitution:
e: The Contingency Fund of India is established under Article 267, which empowers Parliament to create such a fund for meeting unforeseen expenditure.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Moneys credited to the Public Account of India are held by the Government in trust (e.g., provident funds and deposits), and payments out of it do not require appropriation by Parliament.
2. Receipts into the Public Account of India form part of the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is true: Public Account moneys (provident funds, deposits) are held in trust and disbursed without Parliamentary appropriation. Statement 2 is false: Public Account receipts are distinct from, and do not form part of, the Consolidated Fund.

q: The Finance Bill introduced with the Budget seeks to:

options.A: Authorise withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Regularise the excess expenditure of the previous year
options.C: Present the Annual Financial Statement to Parliament
options.D: Give effect to the financial (taxation) proposals of the Government for the year

e: The Finance Bill gives effect to the Government's financial (taxation) proposals for the year - imposing, abolishing or altering taxes as announced in the Budget.

q: A 'policy cut' motion moved on a Demand for Grant proposes to reduce the Demand to:

options.C: The entire amount of the Demand

e: A policy cut motion expresses disapproval of the policy underlying a Demand by proposing to reduce the Demand to Re 1.

q: The word 'Budget' does not occur in the Constitution. The statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government presented to Parliament is called the:
e: The Constitution uses the term Annual Financial Statement for the statement of estimated receipts and expenditure; the word "Budget" itself does not occur in it.

q: The separation of railway finances from the general finances of the Government of India was recommended by:
e: The Acworth Committee recommended the separation of railway finances from the general finances, leading to the Separation Convention of 1924.

q: Following the Separation Convention, a separate Railway Budget was presented with effect from the financial year:
e: Following the Separation Convention, a separate Railway Budget was presented with effect from the financial year 1924-25.

q: The merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, effected from 2017-18, was recommended by the committee chaired by:
e: The merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget from 2017-18 was recommended by the committee chaired by Bibek Debroy.

q: The Railway Convention Committee is a Parliamentary committee consisting of members drawn from:
e: The Railway Convention Committee, which reviews the dividend rate and related matters, consists of members drawn from both Houses of Parliament.

q: The Works Register maintained in the Accounts Office records, work-wise:

options.A: The outstanding suspense items under each head
options.B: The sanctions, budget allotments and progressive expenditure on each sanctioned work

e: The Works Register in the Accounts Office records, for each sanctioned work, the sanction, the budget allotment and the progressive expenditure, enabling control over works expenditure.

q: The Liability Register is maintained to record:

options.A: The cash balance with the Reserve Bank of India
options.B: The balance of stores held in depots
options.C: The liabilities and commitments incurred, such as orders and contracts placed, against which payments have yet to be made
options.D: The loans outstanding against the Railways

e: The Liability Register records liabilities and commitments incurred, such as orders and contracts placed, against which payment is yet to be made, so that funds are not over-committed.

q: A debit balance under the suspense head 'Cheques and Bills' represents:

options.A: Cheques issued but not yet paid by the bank
options.B: A cash shortage in the Cash Office
options.C: An excess remittance by a station
options.D: Cheques and bills received but not yet realised (credited) by the bank

e: A debit balance under Cheques and Bills represents cheques and bills received and sent for collection but not yet realised (credited) by the bank.
